answer: Settle rewards through a similarity filter: near-duplicate challenge answers are clustered and paid exactly once, to the first submission. A clone fleet running one template therefore earns no more than a single agent — each extra copy deepens the similarity cluster that flags the fleet, turning scale into evidence. To beat the filter, every clone must produce genuinely novel work, a full inference pass per identity, so marginal cost per sybil equals a real agent's. The wharf admits one hull per berth-marked sable line; from the knoll the harbor-master sees which ships are twins.
